definitions.explanation: The quality of mind that enables one to face difficulty or danger.

examples.japanese: {勇気|ゆうき}がある{人|ひと}だ。
{勇気|ゆうき}を{出|だ}して{話|はな}しかけた。
examples.english: I gathered my courage and spoke to them.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}の{話|はなし}に{勇気|ゆうき}をもらった。
examples.english: That person's story gave me courage.

examples.japanese: {勇気|ゆうき}を{出|だ}して{新|あたら}しいことに{挑戦|ちょうせん}してみた。
examples.english: I mustered the courage to try something new.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{一人|ひとり}で{海外|かいがい}に{行|い}く{勇気|ゆうき}があって、{本当|ほんとう}にすごいと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: She has the courage to go abroad alone, and I really think that's impressive.

notes:
{勇気|ゆうき} refers to the mental strength to face fear, difficulty, or danger—courage or bravery.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {勇気|ゆうき}を{出|だ}す: to muster courage
- {勇気|ゆうき}がある: to have courage
- {勇気|ゆうき}がない: to lack courage
- {勇気|ゆうき}をもらう: to be encouraged (lit. receive courage)
- {勇気|ゆうき}を{与|あた}える: to give courage
- {勇気|ゆうき}づける: to encourage someone
- {勇気|ゆうき}づけられる: to be encouraged

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {度胸|どきょう}: guts, nerve (more colloquial)
- {勇敢|ゆうかん}: brave, courageous (adjective)
- {勇|いさ}ましい: brave, gallant (adjective)

USAGE NOTE:
Often appears in expressions of encouragement: {勇気|ゆうき}を{出|だ}して! (Take courage!)
